### NAME

`picklescan` - Picklescan — static security scanner for pickle/PyTorch model files: flags dangerous globals and unsafe opcodes.

### SYNOPSIS & usage

*Derived from the upstream README at generation
time; verify against `--help` where the tool is
installed.*

```
pip install picklescan
picklescan --huggingface ykilcher/totally-harmless-model
```

```
https://huggingface.co/ykilcher/totally-harmless-model/resolve/main/pytorch_model.bin:archive/data.pkl: global import '__builtin__ eval' FOUND
----------- SCAN SUMMARY -----------
Scanned files: 1
Infected files: 1
Dangerous globals: 1
```

### DESCRIPTION (upstream)

Security scanner detecting Python Pickle files performing suspicious actions. Scan a malicious model on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/): pip install picklescan picklescan --huggingface ykilcher/totally-harmless-model The scanner reports that the Pickle is calling `eval()` to execute arbitrary code: https://huggingface.co/ykilcher/totally-harmless-model/resolve/main/pytorch_model.bin:archive/data.pkl: global import '__builtin__ eval' FOUND Scanned files: 1 Infected files: 1 Dangerous globals: 1 The scanner can also load Pickles from local files, directories, URLs, and zip archives (a-la [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/)): picklescan --path downloads/pytorch_model.bin picklescan --path d
